topics.title: General Science – Biology
topics.concept: Cells, biomolecules, human body systems, diversity of life, adaptation and plants (Biology textbooks G9–G12).

subtopics.title: Cells and cell transport
subtopics.concept: Prokaryotes lack a membrane-bound nucleus but have ribosomes, a cell wall, often a capsule and pili. Mitochondria – cellular respiration. Plant cells (not animal cells) have chloroplasts, cell walls and a large vacuole. Diffusion needs no ATP (passive transport). Cytology = study of cells.

subtopics.title: Biomolecules, ATP and nucleic acids
subtopics.concept: Amino acids are the units of proteins. ATP is the immediate energy source and energy carrier made by all organisms. Carbohydrates: potatoes, cereals, wheat, milk (lactose). DNA carries hereditary information; RNA has A, U, C and G. Transcription makes mRNA from DNA. Alcoholic fermentation: glucose → ethanol + CO₂ + energy.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 3 – Metabolic Processes and Energy Transfers in Living Organisms

subtopics.title: Circulation, blood and defence
subtopics.concept: Blood flows arteries → capillaries → veins; arteries branch into smaller arterioles; capillary walls are one cell thick. Red blood cells are the most numerous cells. First line of defence: skin, mucus, cilia, tears, saliva; white blood cells are the second line. Lymph nodes lie in the cervical, axillary, thoracic and pelvic regions – not in the central nervous system.

textbook_refs.section: 2.1 The heart – heartbeat and blood pressure

subtopics.title: Human body systems
subtopics.concept: Skin: protection/immunity, excretion (sweat), homeostasis (temperature), sensing. Kidneys: remove wastes, regulate water, salts and pH. Thyroxine regulates metabolism; ovaries make oestrogen and progesterone; LH makes the corpus luteum secrete progesterone. Appendicular skeleton: limbs and girdles (femur). Retina has rods (dim light) and cones (bright light, colour). Ganglion = clump of neuron cell bodies. Urethra carries urine and semen.

subtopics.title: Bacteria and classification
subtopics.concept: Bacteria live everywhere – air, water, soil, hot springs, ocean floor, on and in organisms. Plantae: bryophytes (non-vascular), pteridophytes (true roots, stems, leaves), gymnosperms (naked seeds), angiosperms (flowering plants). Sponges belong to kingdom Animalia.

textbook_refs.section: 2.1 The importance of classification – levels of classification

subtopics.title: Adaptation
subtopics.concept: Adaptation: an inherited modification of structure or function that increases fitness in a stressful environment; strategies: escape, avoidance, tolerance; without adaptation species may become extinct.

subtopics.title: Plant tissues and seeds
subtopics.concept: Imbibition = absorption of water by seeds (first step of germination). Parenchyma – most abundant; chlorenchyma – parenchyma with many chloroplasts; collenchyma – living, under the epidermis; sclerenchyma – dead at maturity, support.

textbook_refs.section: 4.2 Adaptations of plants to water – hydrophytes

subtopics.title: Nutrition and digestion
subtopics.concept: Ingestion → digestion → absorption → assimilation → egestion (elimination of undigested food). Peristalsis = wave-like muscular contractions that push the bolus/chyme along the gut. Protein deficiency → kwashiorkor; energy/food deficiency → marasmus; vitamin C → scurvy; iodine → goitre. Lipids (fats) are built from glycerol and fatty acids. The pharynx is shared by the respiratory and digestive systems.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 3 – Metabolic Processes and Energy Transfers in Living Organisms

subtopics.title: Breathing and respiration
subtopics.concept: Inhalation: diaphragm and external intercostal muscles contract, chest volume increases and pressure falls, so air flows in. External respiration = gas exchange with the environment; internal (cellular) respiration = energy release in cells.

subtopics.title: Nucleic acids, cell division and inheritance
subtopics.concept: A nucleotide = one pentose sugar + one phosphate + one nitrogenous base; the sugar–phosphate chain is the backbone. Prophase: chromatin condenses into chromosomes, nucleolus and nuclear membrane disappear. Meiosis gives four haploid (n), genetically different cells. Genotype = genetic make-up (e.g. TtHH). ABO blood groups: multiple alleles Iᴬ, Iᴮ, i; Iᴬ and Iᴮ are co-dominant.

subtopics.title: Homeostasis, excretion and hormones
subtopics.concept: Kidney (nephron = functional unit) controls water and salt balance; deamination of excess amino acids happens in the liver. Aldosterone regulates blood volume (Na⁺ reabsorption); ADH (vasopressin) water reabsorption. Heat gain: vasoconstriction, hair erection, shivering, adrenaline/thyroxine; sweating is heat loss. Excess iron → haemochromatosis. The pituitary is the 'master gland'.

subtopics.title: Evolution and speciation
subtopics.concept: Neo-Darwinism = the synthetic theory of evolution (Darwin's natural selection + genetics). Genetic isolating mechanisms: habitat, mechanical, behavioural, seasonal, gametic mortality, zygotic mortality, hybrid inviability/sterility → speciation.

subtopics.title: Ecology and natural cycles
subtopics.concept: Abiotic factors: water, soil, light, temperature, pH, minerals; biotic factors: living organisms. Water cycle: evaporation, transpiration (water loss from plants), condensation, precipitation.

subtopics.title: Characteristics of life, branches of biology and cell theory
subtopics.concept: Characteristics of life: metabolism, growth and development (birth → growth → maturity → senility → death), responsiveness, homeostasis, reproduction. Branches: morphology (form), physiology (function), cytology (cells), taxonomy (classification), genetics (heredity). Cell theory: all living things are made up of cells; the cell is the basic unit of life; cells come from pre-existing cells.

subtopics.title: Reproduction and birth control
subtopics.concept: Asexual reproduction in animals: budding (hydra), regeneration, parthenogenesis (unfertilised egg develops); binary fission is typical of bacteria and protists. Male ducts: epididymis → vas deferens → urethra; the ovaries produce eggs (ova) and hormones. Birth control: abstinence, rhythm method, condoms, spermicidal creams and foaming tablets, pills, IUD, sterilisation.

topics.title: General Science – Chemistry
topics.concept: Matter, atoms and the periodic table, bonding, stoichiometry, acids and bases, energy and rates, metals and non-metals, gases, organic and nuclear chemistry (Chemistry textbooks G9–G12).

subtopics.title: Matter, mixtures, separation and changes
subtopics.concept: Chemistry is applied in medicines, plastics, cement, food preservation and pesticides. Heterogeneous mixtures (oil and water) are not uniform. A magnet separates iron from sulphur. Burning and rusting are chemical changes; condensation and melting are physical changes. Steel = iron + carbon. Coal is not an element.

subtopics.title: Atoms, symbols and the periodic table
subtopics.concept: Cobalt = Co. Group VIIIA (18) = noble gases. Number of electrons of a neutral atom = atomic number (²⁴₁₂Mg has 12). Ionisation energy increases across a period and decreases down a group (Cl > I, Na > K). Non-metals: poor conductors, brittle, high electronegativity, low density – not ductile.

subtopics.title: Bonding, shapes and allotropes
subtopics.concept: Covalent bond = sharing of electrons between non-metals; ionic bond = transfer (MgO). H₂O is bent (V-shaped). Allotropes of carbon (diamond, graphite) differ in the arrangement of their carbon atoms.

subtopics.title: Moles, molar mass, molality and gas volume
subtopics.concept: Molar mass Ca(NO₃)₂ = 164 g/mol. n = m/M. Molality m = moles of solute / kg of solvent. At constant T and P, V ∝ n (Avogadro's law).

subtopics.title: Acids, bases and electrolytes
subtopics.concept: Gastric juice contains HCl (acid). Strong acids: HCl, HNO₃, H₂SO₄; strong bases: NaOH, KOH, Ca(OH)₂. Strong electrolytes ionise completely (H₂SO₄). Diprotic acid: two acidic H (H₂SO₄).

subtopics.title: Energy, rates, enthalpy, oxidation numbers and reaction types
subtopics.concept: Kinetic forms: thermal, electrical; potential forms: chemical, gravitational. Rate = change in concentration with time (increase of product or decrease of reactant). ΔH = H(products) − H(reactants). S in SO₄²⁻ is +6. AB + CD → AD + CB is double displacement (precipitation).

subtopics.title: Uses and occurrence of elements and compounds
subtopics.concept: KI (iodised salt) prevents iodine deficiency. Aluminium ore = bauxite. CO₂: photosynthesis, fire extinguishers, carbonated drinks, dry-ice refrigeration. Unreactive metals (Au, Pt) occur free in nature.

subtopics.title: Gas laws
subtopics.concept: Boyle's law: at constant temperature the pressure of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its volume (PV = constant). Avogadro's law: V ∝ n at constant T and P.

subtopics.title: Hydrocarbons and nuclear reactions
subtopics.concept: Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ (C₈H₁₈); alkenes CₙH₂ₙ undergo addition, are insoluble in water and burn to CO₂ and H₂O. Nuclear reactions involve loss of mass, are irreversible and their rate is not affected by temperature.

topics.title: General Science – Physics
topics.concept: Units and vectors, motion, work–energy–power, heat, moments, electricity and magnetism, optics, waves, fluids and quantum physics (Physics textbooks G9–G12).

subtopics.title: Units, vectors and displacement
subtopics.concept: Energy units: joule, erg, kWh, watt-second, MJ (dyne/cm is a surface-tension unit). The resultant of two vectors is largest (A + B) when the angle between them is 0° and smallest at 180°. Displacement adds as vectors (Pythagoras for perpendicular parts).

subtopics.title: Motion: free fall, graphs and circular motion
subtopics.concept: Free fall from rest: h = ½gt², so g = 2h/t² (need height and time). A parabolic distance–time graph means uniform acceleration. Non-uniform circular motion has tangential and radial (centripetal) acceleration.

textbook_refs.section: 3.3 Newton's first law of motion – inertia

subtopics.title: Work, energy, power and collisions
subtopics.concept: W = Fd; P = W/t = mgh/t; spring energy = ½kx². Elastic collision: momentum and kinetic energy conserved; inelastic: only momentum.

subtopics.title: Heat and states of matter
subtopics.concept: Q = mcΔT. A pure solid melts at a definite temperature (melting point); impurities change boiling points; evaporation depends on temperature, pressure, surface area and wind; sublimation = solid ↔ gas.

subtopics.title: Moments and equilibrium
subtopics.concept: Principle of moments: sum of clockwise moments = sum of anticlockwise moments about the pivot (F₁d₁ = F₂d₂).

subtopics.title: Electricity and magnetism
subtopics.concept: Two equal resistors in parallel: R/2. Q = It. F = BIL sin θ on a current-carrying conductor. Transformers (AC only, laminated soft-iron core) change voltage, not power (Vs/Vp = Ns/Np). Magnets attract only ferromagnetic materials (iron, nickel, cobalt).

subtopics.title: Light, mirrors and lenses
subtopics.concept: Pinhole camera: real, inverted image (diminished when the screen is nearer than the object). Concave mirror, object beyond C: real, inverted, diminished image between F and C. Lens power P = 1/f (f in m). Compound microscope: final image virtual, magnified, inverted.

subtopics.title: Waves
subtopics.concept: Mechanical waves need a medium and transfer energy, not matter. v = fλ. In refraction speed and wavelength change; frequency (and period) stay the same.

subtopics.title: Pressure and relative density
subtopics.concept: Pressure at a point in a liquid acts equally in all directions and increases with depth (p = hρg). Relative density = density of substance / density of water. Balanced liquid columns: h₁ρ₁ = h₂ρ₂.

subtopics.title: Photons and X-rays
subtopics.concept: Photon energy E = hf = hc/λ; λ(nm) ≈ 1240/E(eV). Shortest X-ray wavelength λmin = hc/(eV) for accelerating voltage V.
